title: Conception and pregnancy in adults with chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) in the era of tyrosine kinase inhibitors: retrospective survey on the course and outcome of pregnancies and on therapy and disease control in CML
summary:
Only about 20 years ago, a innovative new drug was developed for the treatment of chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML), which specifically inhibits the biological processes that cause CML. It belongs to a group of drugs that are known as tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). Five TKIs are now marketed for the treatment of CML, with different efficacy and toxicity profiles. TKIs have drastically prolonged the survival times of CML patients and are now standard therapy. 
However, in studies on animals prior to the approval of TKIs, damage to the descendants and complications in pregnancy were observed in some cases. With some TKIs, an impairment of fertility was also observed. The manufacturers of TKIs therefore urgently advise against becoming pregnant during treatment with TKIs and in some cases also against fathering a child as a man. Taking TKIs during the first 12 weeks of pregnancy is particularly risky, as the child's organs are forming during this time. Some manufacturers also recommend thinking about conserving ovum or sperm cells so that they can be used later to conceive a child. 

We would like to know how patients with chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) are currently treated before, during and after a planned or unplanned pregnancy and what impact this has on disease control of CML. We also still know little about whether and to what extent therapies with the various currently available CML drugs affect fertility, the course of pregnancy or the health of the unborn child in humans. Furthermore, we would like to find out whether and to what extent CML patients and patients who wish to have children or are of childbearing age are advised by their physicians. 
Male and female persons with CML who have been pregnant or have conceived a child since the approval of TKI (November 2001) are asked to fill out once questionnaires on the above-mentioned topics and/or to provide copies of doctor's letters, findings, etc. and/or to allow the data to be obtained directly from their treating physicians (release from the duty of confidentiality).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written informed consent to study participation. 
- age ≥ 18 years
- Diagnosis of CML (detection of Philadelphia chromosome or CML fusion gene) or conception with a man with confirmed CML diagnosis treated with TKI or  < 1 month after the end of TKI therapy
- Pregnancies in female CML-patients  that existed at the time of CML diagnosis or occurred thereafter since 11/2001, or fathering  by male CML patients after diagnosis of CML since 11/2001
- TreatmentL with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) before, during, or after pregnancy, or before or during fathering.
Exclusion criteria:
No exclusion criteria
